SRDatalog Language Macros

This module provides the main DSL (Domain-Specific Language) macros for writing Datalog programs in Nim. These macros translate Nim syntax into C++ code that uses the SRDatalog runtime library.

Overview

The SRDatalog Nim wrapper provides a high-level, type-safe interface for writing Datalog programs. It uses Nim's powerful macro system to generate optimized C++ code at compile time, combining the expressiveness of Nim with the performance of the C++ runtime.

Main Macros

  • srdatalog_prelude(): Initializes the SRDatalog environment and includes necessary C++ headers
  • datalog_db: Defines a database schema with relation declarations
  • none_recursive_rule: Defines non-recursive Datalog rules
  • edb: Adds extensional database (EDB) facts to a database

Example Usage

import srdatalog/lang

srdatalog_prelude()

datalog_db MyDB:
  RRel: Relation[int, int]
  SRel: Relation[int, int, int]

none_recursive_rule MyRule:
  [{(ZRel x y z)} <--
    {(RRel x y) (SRel y z h)}
  ] {. name: Triangle order: [x, y, z] .}

var arena = newArena()
var db = SemiNaiveDatabase(...)

edb db:
  (RRel ($"BooleanSR::one()") ($"1") ($"2"))
  (SRel ($"BooleanSR::one()") ($"2") ($"3") ($"4"))

See also

For more details on the C++ runtime, see the C++ documentation in relation_col.h, runtime.h, and query.h.

Macros

macro datalog_db(db_name: untyped; decls: untyped): untyped

Defines a Datalog database schema with relation declarations.

This macro generates C++ type aliases for relation schemas and a database blueprint that groups all relations together.

Parameters:

  • db_name: The name of the database (identifier)
  • decls: A block of relation declarations in the format: RelName: Relation[Type1, Type2, ...] or RelName: Semiring[Type1, Type2, ..., SemiringType]

Each relation declaration specifies:

  • RelName: The name of the relation (must be a valid identifier)
  • Relation[...]: For relations using the default Boolean semiring
  • Semiring[...]: For relations with a custom semiring (last parameter)

The macro generates:

  • Type aliases for each relation schema
  • A database blueprint type that groups all relations

Example:

datalog_db TriangleDB:
  RRel: Relation[int, int]
  SRel: Relation[int, int, int]
  # This generates:
  # using namespace SRDatalog::AST::literals;
  # using RRel = AST::RelationSchema<decltype("RRel"_s), BooleanSR, int, int>;
  # using SRel = AST::RelationSchema<decltype("SRel"_s), BooleanSR, int, int, int>;
  # using TriangleDB = AST::Database<RRel, SRel>;
macro edb(db_name: untyped; facts_raw: untyped): untyped

Adds extensional database (EDB) facts to a database.

EDB facts are ground facts (concrete tuples) that are explicitly added to the database, as opposed to intensional database (IDB) facts that are derived by rules.

Parameters:

  • db_name: The name of the database variable to add facts to
  • facts_raw: A sequence of fact definitions, each in the format: (RelName ($"annotation") ($"arg1") ($"arg2") ...)

Fact syntax:

  • RelName: The relation name (must match a relation in the database schema)
  • Annotation: Semiring annotation value (e.g., $"BooleanSR::one()")
  • Arguments: C++ code strings for each attribute value

Each fact is converted to a call to add_fact<RelName>(db, annotation, arg1, arg2, ...).

Example:

edb triangle_runtime:
  (RRel ($"BooleanSR::one()") ($"1") ($"10"))
  (RRel ($"BooleanSR::one()") ($"2") ($"20"))
  (SRel ($"BooleanSR::one()") ($"10") ($"7") ($"5"))
Note: The $"..." syntax creates C++ string literals that are emitted directly into the generated C++ code. Use this for C++ expressions like semiring values and numeric literals.

macro fixpoint_rule(rule_name: untyped; rules: untyped): untyped

Defines fixpoint (recursive) Datalog rules.

This macro generates C++ code for fixpoint rule sets. Fixpoint rules are recursive rules where the head relation can appear in the body, enabling iterative computation until a fixed point is reached.

Parameters:

  • rule_name: The name of the fixpoint rule set (identifier)
  • rules: A sequence of rule definitions with the same syntax as none_recursive_rule, but where the head relation may appear in the body

Rule syntax:

  • Head: {(RelName var1 var2 ...)} - defines what relation is computed
  • Body: {(RelName1 var1 var2) (RelName2 var2 var3) ...} - defines join conditions
  • Variables: Logical variables that appear in both head and body
  • Pragma `name`: Required name for the rule
  • Pragma `order`: Required join order (list of variables)

The macro automatically generates multiple rule variants for semi-naive evaluation. For each rule where an incremental relation appears in the body, it creates variants that use DELTA_VER for that relation and FULL_VER for others.

The macro generates:

  • C++ type aliases for each rule variant
  • A Fixpoint type grouping all rule variants
  • Rule variant lists for efficient semi-naive evaluation

Example:

fixpoint_rule TransitiveClosure:
  [{(Path x z)} <--
    {(Path x y) (Edge y z)}
  ] {. name: TCTransitive order: [y, x, z] .}

This generates rule variants that use DELTA_VER for Path in the body when computing new Path facts, enabling efficient incremental computation.

Note: Fixpoint rules require the database to be initialized with memory arenas for semi-naive evaluation (full, delta, and new versions).
macro none_recursive_rule(rule_name: untyped; rules: untyped): untyped

Defines non-recursive Datalog rules.

This macro generates C++ code for non-recursive rule sets. Non-recursive rules are rules where the head relation does not appear in the body (no self-reference).

Parameters:

  • rule_name: The name of the rule set (identifier)
  • rules: A sequence of rule definitions, each with:
    • Head clause(s) in curly braces: {(RelName arg1 arg2 ...)}
    • Body clause(s) in curly braces: {(RelName arg1 arg2 ...)}
    • Arrow operator: <-- separating head from body
    • Pragma annotations: {. name: RuleName order: [var1, var2, ...] .}

Rule syntax:

  • Head: {(RelName var1 var2 ...)} - defines what relation is computed
  • Body: {(RelName1 var1 var2) (RelName2 var2 var3) ...} - defines join conditions
  • Variables: Logical variables that appear in both head and body
  • Pragma `name`: Required name for the rule
  • Pragma `order`: Required join order (list of variables)

The macro generates:

  • C++ type aliases for each rule
  • MIR (Mid-level Intermediate Representation) compilation for each rule
  • A NonIterativeRuleSets type grouping all rules

Example:

none_recursive_rule TriangleRule:
  [{(ZRel x y z)} <--
    {(RRel x y) (SRel y z h) (TRel z x f)}
  ] {. name: Triangle order: [x, y, z] .}
macro print_ast(ast: untyped): untyped

Debug macro for printing AST (Abstract Syntax Tree) representations.

This macro is useful for debugging and understanding how the macro system parses and transforms Datalog syntax.

Parameters:

  • ast: The AST node to print

Prints the string representation of the AST node to stdout. Useful for debugging macro transformations.

Note: This is a development/debugging tool and may not be needed in production code.
macro srdatalog_prelude(): untyped

Initializes the SRDatalog environment.

This macro must be called before using any other SRDatalog macros. It:

  • Includes necessary C++ headers (ast.h, query.h, runtime.h, semiring.h)
  • Sets up the SRDatalog namespace
  • Defines the Arena type for memory management
  • Provides the newArena() function for creating memory arenas

Example:

srdatalog_prelude()
# Now you can use datalog_db, none_recursive_rule, etc.
